current_activity: regiment in the invasion sector west of Bayeux, detached from the corps
notes: Event date: 6 June 1944 (FMS B-597, the 20 September 1944 corps report, p.-4-: at the start of the invasion Flaksturmregiment 1 stood in the invasion sector in the area west of Bayeux and was hit especially hard). Event definition: the regiment, detached from the corps at the end of May 1944 because of heavy air attacks in the area, was west of Bayeux on the first day of the invasion; it came back to the corps only several weeks after the invasion began (R2216 ms -34-). Event support: one source family (FMS: the corps report and Pickert's 1947 manuscript, which calls it the 4th regiment, counting, and puts it at Bayeux-Isigny; the comment in the same file has one regiment of the corps north of Isigny protecting the artillery group there). Location: Bayeux (place PL0033) with the qualifier area west of and a precision of 25 km. Written exception to G9 (10 km): the Anlage 2 sketch (5 June 1944 evening) and the comment put the regiment at or north of Isigny-sur-Mer, about 27 km west of Bayeux, so the precision is widened to take them in (Scott accepted B-597 Q7, 23 November 2026). Location support: the corps report names the area west of Bayeux; Holm (R1938, Flak-Sturm-Regiment 1 page) has it between Isigny and Bayeux in May-June 1944 (a two-town area, no claim, G9), which agrees. Review: confidence 0.3 from the rubric (G9: area given by one named town (0.3)); added in the FMS B-597 pass (branch fms-b597, 23 November 2026): old value none, new value this claim; parent_unit_id old value none, new value blank, reason: parents are left blank on claim rows (the chain is in the command relations); Scott accepted B-597 Q7 (23 November 2026). Context: B-597 identifies the regiment by number only in the corps report; Pickert's "4. Regt." is an ordinal, not Flak-Sturm-Regiment 4. Bayeux fell to the British on 7 June 1944 (C0044). Activity: in_line, span point, stated (the regiment was in the invasion sector and was hit especially hard).

notes: Event date: 24 June 1944 (Holm, day date of the battalion re-formation). Location support: Holm names Bayeux for the regiment (June-August 1944) and for the re-formation of its battalions. Review: confidence 0.3 from the rubric (G-b/L7: inferred place for the regiment staff from its battalions and its own June-August row (0.3)); added in the Luftwaffe ground G-b pass (branch normandy-lw-ground-b, 19 November 2026): old value none, new value this claim; parent_unit_id old value none, new value blank, reason: parents are left blank on claim rows (the chain is in the command relations). Context: Inferred: old value none, new value Bayeux on 24 June 1944, reason: the regiment row is an area with two names over three months (G9), and the only dated fact is the re-formation of both battalions at Bayeux. Bayeux was in Allied hands from 7 June 1944, so Holm's "Bayeux" is read as the Bayeux area rather than the town (0.3).
